processSteps.label: Dry the harvest
processSteps.claim: Mature rye drops wet grain bundles under the installed crop patch. Shift-right-click bundles onto the ground and wait for them to dry.

processSteps.label: Thresh and allocate
processSteps.claim: Use a stick on a placed dry bundle stack to separate grains from straw. Keep seeds for replanting. The knife-plus-rye-seed crafting recipe yields rye grain for the kitchen.

processSteps.label: Feed appropriately
processSteps.claim: Fill a trough with feed suitable for the animal species. Rye seeds can go into the large trough; check each animal’s diet rather than assuming every animal eats them.

processSteps.label: Maintain living conditions
processSteps.claim: Keep animals clean, sheltered and watered; welfare can affect survival, milk and fibre. To milk an eligible animal, target it directly with a compatible liquid container rather than the adjacent block.

processSteps.label: Do not impose disabled breeding rules
processSteps.claim: Livestock Welfare’s breeding module is disabled: its bedding and pregnancy settings are not extra requirements. This does not disable animal breeding. GeneLib and species behaviours still matter; do not apply one species’ genetics or manure timing to every animal.

processSteps.label: Return nutrients
processSteps.claim: Turn appropriate manure into slurry and compost in barrels, then use the listed fertilizer recipes to restore field nutrients. Different animals need not supply the same ingredients.

processSteps.label: Bring the body home
processSteps.claim: Right-click a supported dead animal to carry it in a free bag slot; small bodies fit ordinary inventory slots. Bring it home promptly: field harvesting sacrifices yield.

processSteps.label: Skin and bleed
processSteps.claim: Place the body on a skinning hook. Hold right-click with a knife to skin it; wait for its bled-out color before removing it. Work promptly because bodies rot on stations.

processSteps.label: Butcher and sort
processSteps.claim: Put the bled-out body on a butchering table and process it with a knife or cleaver. Break the remaining bone carcass for bones. Send meat to cooking/preservation and skins to the appropriate hide recipes.

processSteps.label: Render fat
processSteps.claim: Cook two raw primemeat with two litres of water in a pot to obtain one rendered fat. Keep rendered fat for the recipes that ask for it; it is not interchangeable with every other fat ingredient.

processSteps.label: Soak and scrape
processSteps.claim: Make limewater from lime and water. Seal a compatible raw hide in the limewater recipe. Craft the soaked hide with a knife in the grid to obtain scraped hide; species-specific recipes convert supported skins to size-based scraped hides.

processSteps.label: Tan twice
processSteps.claim: Make weak tannin from tanning bark and water, then strong tannin from tanning bark and weak tannin. Seal scraped hide in weak tannin to prepare it, then seal prepared hide in strong tannin. Vanilla log-to-tannin recipes are disabled here; use the bark recipes for quantities and sealing times.

processSteps.label: Use leather
processSteps.claim: Use plain normal leather in the relevant equipment recipe. Sewn body/leg armor also requires flax twine. Do not substitute pelts or arbitrary species skins for generic tanning ingredients.

processSteps.label: Establish bees
processSteps.claim: Use the skep route to obtain a populated colony, then move it to a flower-rich apiary. Keep that occupied skep for populating upgraded hives.

processSteps.label: Build a ceramic hive
processSteps.claim: Clay-form and fire a ceramic brood pot and hive top. Transfer the skep colony to the pot and attach the top. The hive retains its colony through the top-harvesting cycle. Interacting with the brood pot while holding the populated skep consumes the skep.

processSteps.label: Harvest and reset
processSteps.claim: When the top is ready, remove it and use a knife to harvest the comb; replace the emptied top. Process comb for honey and wax without destroying the populated brood pot.

processSteps.label: Prepare Langstroth frames
processSteps.claim: Build the base, supers, brood box and rack from the native Langstroth guide. Wax linen and cut it into frame liners; fit liners to empty frames on the rack before production.

processSteps.label: Assemble and repeat
processSteps.claim: Put lined frames in supers, close them and stack them on the base; add the populated brood box on top. Harvest ready frames on the rack with a knife, repair as instructed, then return frames and hive parts.

processSteps.label: Integrate with fields
processSteps.claim: The installed pollination guide describes benefits for nearby crops, berries and fruit trees. Use that native guide instead of assuming vanilla-only bee behavior or one universal effective radius.

processSteps.label: Dry and thresh flax
processSteps.claim: Mature flax drops wet grain bundles. Place and dry them, then thresh the dry stack with a stick. Reserve the recovered flax seed; keep dry flax straw for fiber.

processSteps.label: Ret, rinse and soften
processSteps.claim: Soak dry straw in fresh water. Rinse wet straw using the installed water-container or barrel recipe to obtain clean straw. Hold right-click with clean straw to crumple it, then process crumpled straw with a ridge in the offhand to separate fiber.

processSteps.label: Spin and weave linen
processSteps.claim: Tailor’s Delight adds spindle-assisted flax twine. Four twine around a stick make plain cloth; plain cloth converts to a normal linen block and returns the stick. Respect any displayed class requirement.

processSteps.label: Shear and wash fleece
processSteps.claim: The native guide requires living generation-one-or-higher animals and recommends shears; knives risk injury. Wash generic plain fleece with 0.5 litre limewater for 18 hours to obtain generic plain fibers. Species and colors are separate variants.

processSteps.label: Spin and weave wool
processSteps.claim: Spin the washed fibres into wool twine with the spindle recipe. Twine plus a stick makes portable wool cloth; the square-twine recipe makes a wool block. Use the form named by your garment recipe.

processSteps.label: Sew the selected garment
processSteps.claim: Dressmakers recipes may require dyed cloth, leather bundles, colored twine and an awl. The pack enables common/class/Nadiyan clothing and wool alternatives; this is not removal of clothier trait gates.

processSteps.label: Set up simmering
processSteps.claim: Put a fired saucepan into a firepit. Its four ingredient slots are for simmering, not ordinary cooking-pot meals. Add the recipe's liquid and solid ingredients in matching numbers of portions. A cauldron is an alternative station.

processSteps.label: Make the stock
processSteps.claim: Simmer one bone with 1 L water to produce 0.5 L bone broth. Liquid output stays inside the saucepan: take the filled saucepan from the firepit output before pouring or using it again.

processSteps.label: Choose clarified broth
processSteps.claim: For clarification, simmer 0.1 L bone broth with 0.01 L egg white to make 0.1 L clarified bone broth. Do not substitute a bone for the egg white; that belongs to the gelatin branch.

processSteps.label: Or continue to gelatin
processSteps.claim: Save unclarified broth for this route. Simmer 1 L bone broth with another bone to obtain liquid gelatin. Simmer 10 liquid-gelatin portions with a bone and 1 L water to obtain raw gelatin; simmer that raw gelatin with 1 L water for plain gelatin. Solid outputs can be taken directly from the output slot.

processSteps.label: Knead, without a cooking pot
processSteps.claim: Place a mixing bowl and open it with right-click. Add one flour and 0.1 L liquid whole egg or yolk to its ingredient slots. Leave the cooking-pot slot empty: this is kneading an item, not mixing a meal. Hold right-click on the bowl to produce pasta dough.

processSteps.label: Flatten and cut
processSteps.claim: In the crafting grid, put a stone above the pasta dough to make a sheet; a hammer or rolling pin is another option. Combine the sheet with a knife or cleaver to cut noodles.

processSteps.label: Dry the surplus
processSteps.claim: Bake cut noodles in an oven until they become dried pasta, then remove them before they char. Drying is a real preservation step: dried noodles have a much longer base freshness period than fresh noodles, and still work in the simmering recipe.

processSteps.label: Cook when needed
processSteps.claim: Simmer one cut or dried pasta with 1 L water in a saucepan to make cooked pasta. Add cooked pasta to stew or use a mixing-bowl meal recipe. For mixing a meal, unlike kneading dough, put a cooking pot in the bowl's lower-left slot and use the recipe's exact proportions.

processSteps.label: Let the milk separate
processSteps.claim: Seal fresh milk in a barrel in multiples of 10 L. After 24 in-game hours it becomes separating milk. Make a cream scoop from a fired bowl and stick. Pasteurization is separate: cook vanilla milk in a container for Expanded Foods pasteurized milk.

processSteps.label: Skim carefully
processSteps.claim: Crouch with the cream scoop in hand and interact with the barrel. Keep going until skimming finishes; interrupting can mix the milk back together. The scoop collects cream and leaves skim milk in the barrel. Skim milk remains a cooking ingredient, but cannot become cheddar. Skim milk and whey also enter Expanded Foods kneading recipes; that does not make milk interchangeable with water in Manual Dough.

processSteps.label: Churn the cream
processSteps.claim: Craft and place a plunger churn. Click its lower body to open the inventory, put cream in the top slot, then work the handle. Collect unsalted butter from the lower slot. You do not need a cooking pot or a saucepan for this step.

processSteps.label: Salt the stored portion
processSteps.claim: Combine two unsalted butter with one salt in the grid to get two salted butter. One salted butter plus another salt makes twice-salted butter. Each salt stage increases the base freshness period, but neither stops spoilage. Keep butter cool and use the displayed freshness rather than assuming a fixed shelf life.

processSteps.label: Make the container
processSteps.claim: Use a saw with a glass slab in the crafting grid to make four glass bottles. Each bottle holds 1 L and transfers liquid in 0.1 L portions. Fill an open bottle with the liquid ingredient you want to keep before sealing it.

processSteps.label: Prepare corks
processSteps.claim: Simmer dry oak bark with water in a saucepan to make boiled bark. In the crafting grid, put a knife above one boiled bark to make sixteen cork stoppers. This is a kitchen use for bark, separate from the woodworking that supplies your furniture.

processSteps.label: Stopper before storing
processSteps.claim: Insert a stopper into the filled bottle to preserve its contents. Cork is the preservation-focused option. Keep sealed bottles in a cellar, away from temperature swings. Stoppering slows spoilage; it does not make perishable ingredients last forever.

processSteps.label: Open before cooking
processSteps.claim: Unstopper the bottle before drinking or transferring liquid back to your cooking station. Corked and waxed bottle states disable held liquid transfer. Use the open bottle's small transfers to portion liquids for kneading and simmering rather than trying to pour from a sealed bottle.

processSteps.label: 1. Craft scaffolding
processSteps.claim: Open the native recipe: BBB / SRS / S_S, with planks B, sticks S and rope R. It yields four scaffolds. The exported MaxStability=6 is not proof of a safe six-block unsupported span; do not design around that assumption.

processSteps.label: 2. Make and fire shingles
processSteps.claim: Manual Shingle adds right-mouse-button shingle/bowl making. The export specifies three-second batches, two shingles per batch and no required table. Its assets do not establish the exact shingle hand setup, so no brick/sneak instruction is supplied here. Raw red shingles fire to burned red at the native 850°C threshold. Raw blue instead fires to black, not blue.

processSteps.label: 3. Assemble One Roof roofing
processSteps.claim: For red clay use __S / _S_ / S_S: four burned red shingles yield four redclay-standard roof blocks. Separate one-for-one recipes switch standard ↔ dynamic. Use the actual material code, not an invented generic roof-clay. The mod advertises automatic roof building; this export does not explain its placement shortcuts.

processSteps.label: 4. Obtain stone and shape details
processSteps.claim: Stone Harvesting explicitly supports obtaining full rock blocks with hammer and chisel. Saw Chiseling permits wood chiseling with a saw and supplies sawing animation patches. For repeated details open the shipped Chisel Tools guide: the pantograph copies/pastes and saves shapes; the hand planer removes or adds groups of voxels.  Chiseled-block side solidity does not guarantee a sealed, warm or smoke-safe room. Terrain Slabs are a separate recipe branch, not full-block equivalents.

processSteps.label: 1. Build the Heraldry Workbench
processSteps.claim: Gather planks, sticks, resin and plain cloth using the native workbench recipe. Its hammer and chisel are tools with declared durability costs of 20 and 50. Bark Beetle adds an ambient sound to resin-bearing logs and can help locate the resin ingredient.

processSteps.label: 2. Make a base and apply heraldry
processSteps.claim: Both banner and cape recipes use one plank and two plain cloth pieces. Put the product in the workbench input. Its UI identifies liquid containers holding dye, or water as bleach, and separate Patterns/Shapes tabs. Colors/layers are item attributes, not separate red-cape collectible codes. Follow the native dye-making guide for the liquid supply.

processSteps.label: 3. Craft a window and arrange the display
processSteps.claim: Four planks in _A_ / A_A / _A_ yield customwindow-plain. Shared Universal Display Library config documents Raise/lower display item (default Left Shift) + mouse wheel, with a 0.25-voxel step. Precise placement is enabled and item overlap disabled in this export. RoomSafeOpening=false does not establish greenhouse/cellar sealing. Window Display Patches also adjusts placement particles for Pewter lamps.

processSteps.label: 4. Add a chime
processSteps.claim: The wooden wind chime needs rope, one plank and five sticks: _A_ / _B_ / CDC, with two sticks in each C slot and one in D. The copper version uses two bottom slots of two copper rods instead. It is an audio decoration, not a wind meter. Client config controls volume; this export sets main multiplier 3 and maximum distance 16.

processSteps.label: 1. Prepare the alloy and mold
processSteps.claim: Pewter requires tin 80–95%, lead 5–10% and copper 1–5%, all within the same alloy batch. A 90/7/3 split satisfies the recipe. Clayform the Tableware Bowl Mold from blue, red or fire clay using its native pattern, then fire it. Clayforming is not a crafting-grid recipe.

processSteps.label: 2. Cast tableware, then assemble
processSteps.claim: The bowl mold declares 100 metal units and a four-bowl output. A pewter bowl holds one litre or one meal serving. Bowl + candle makes a candlelamp; matching crock base + lid combine shapelessly into a crock. pagoldsilver adds gold and silver variants in the pewter domain, but static variants do not prove that a running mold accepts those melts: check the native item guidance before committing precious metal.

processSteps.label: 3. Stitch an arrow quiver
processSteps.claim: Use the basic LNL / LFL / LLL recipe: plain normal leather, an iron buckle, and an arrow marked as a zero-wear pattern tool rather than a declared consumed ingredient. The output is beltbag-back-quiver-arrows in the quiversandsheaths domain, despite mod ID quiversfork. Asset and exported config indicate three ammunition slots. Colored/material variants change attributes, not this collectible code; this is not a claim of extra ordinary backpack slots.

processSteps.label: Build the firepit
processSteps.claim: Work outdoors or vent smoke to open air: Real Smoke can suffocate players. Gather dry grass and firewood; make a firestarter from two diagonal sticks. Sneak-right-click grass onto solid ground, then add four firewood. Save separate tinder for ignition.

processSteps.label: Kindle separate tinder
processSteps.claim: Sneak-right-click another dry grass onto the ground beside the completed firepit. Aim the firestarter at this separate tinder and sneak-right-click to begin. Keep sneaking, stay still, and alternate left/right clicks until you hold glowing tinder.

processSteps.label: Light the pit
processSteps.claim: Carry the glowing tinder to the completed firepit and right-click it. If ignition is refused, check the environmental warning: Firestarters also imposes weather restrictions on ignition tools.

processSteps.label: Roast on a stick
processSteps.claim: Put roastable raw food in your offhand and a normal stick in your main hand; right-click to skewer it. Hold right-click with the loaded stick aimed at a burning firepit to roast. Empty your offhand and Ctrl-right-click to remove the food.

processSteps.label: Upgrade to pot meals
processSteps.claim: Clay-form and pit-fire a pot and bowl. Put the fired pot in the firepit, fill its ingredient slots with a valid meal recipe and matching portion counts, then cook. Right-click the cooked pot with an empty bowl to serve.

processSteps.label: Wash out leftovers
processSteps.claim: To empty a held meal bowl or cooked container, aim at water and hold right-click for about one second. Washing empties its contents, so finish edible food first. This is an added held interaction, not a requirement to wash every already-empty dish.

processSteps.label: Knead dough
processSteps.claim: Select flour in the active hotbar slot. Put a suitable water-containing item in another hotbar slot, or target a suitable placed water container; hold right-click to knead. Offhand water alone is not sufficient. Grid dough recipes are disabled, including modded dough outputs. Expanded Foods kneading and Core of Arts liquid mixing are separate branches.

processSteps.label: Cure better fuel
processSteps.claim: Shapelessly combine a knife and 2 ordinary firewood for 2 prepared firewood, then let it cure into seasoned fuel; the base curing transition is 96 in-game hours. Alternatively surround resin or beeswax with 8 firewood to craft 8 seasoned firewood directly. The exported pack disables further curing into aged firewood; raw firewood remains allowed for first-fire construction and clay ovens.

processSteps.label: Connect the three oven components
processSteps.claim: Craft Heat Source, Heat Distribution and Baking Space. Put Distribution beside Source, then Baking Space in front of Distribution. This is the Stone Bake Oven layout. A vanilla clay oven is a different branch: DanaTweaks lets a burning firepit directly below heat it.

processSteps.label: Fuel and bake
processSteps.claim: Fuel and torch-light Heat Source; place dough on Baking Space. Heat falls with distance. Vent indoor firepits and smoke-producing heat sources to open air; custom sources may differ. Do not assume a decorative chimney makes a kitchen safe.

processSteps.label: Try an oven pot roast
processSteps.claim: Rustic Cookery is a separate branch: with tongs in your offhand, work a roasting dish on a lit firepit. Render fat, sear a whole meat slab, add sides and braising liquid, then remove the roast and finish it in a preheated clay oven. Place the baked roast and right-click with an empty bowl to serve.

processSteps.label: Brew safe floral tea
processSteps.claim: Use a cooking pot on a lit firepit. For one floral-tea portion, use 1 L water and one cornflower; wild daisy and golden poppy are other listed floral ingredients. Cook to obtain hot floral tea. Do not substitute arbitrary flowers: lily of the valley and the listed lupines produce toxic tea.

processSteps.label: Craft a tankard
processSteps.claim: Use a 2 by 2 grid: stick/plank in the first row, empty/plank in the second. The wooden tankard is a liquid container for tea; it holds 1 L and transfers 0.5 L at a time. Metal tankards and goblets are alternatives, not prerequisites.

processSteps.label: Use hot or cold tea
processSteps.claim: Drink tea hot when practical: the liquid asset gives hot tea a base four-hour freshness period before its cold variant. Cold tea eventually decays back to water. Medicinal tea has a separate ingredient list; toxic tea damages health, so keep it apart from safe drinks.

processSteps.label: Chill food correctly
processSteps.claim: Select shelves and baskets by their accepted contents, not their appearance. Keep the Cooling Cabinet doors closed. Add Cut Ice to its dedicated drawer and close that too: the extra cooling needs both compartments closed. Replace melting ice regularly.

processSteps.label: Maintain an ice reserve
processSteps.claim: Store spare Cut Ice in an Ice Keeper to prevent melting. For baskets inside a cabinet, right-click with accepted food to insert it; Ctrl inserts multiple, while Ctrl with an empty hand removes one item. Read the block tooltip for its actual freshness, curing or drying effect rather than assuming every shelf refrigerates.

processSteps.label: Split your fuel
processSteps.claim: Make a chopping block from a placed log and an axe. Place wood on it with right-click, then hold right-click with an axe to chop. Keep fuel separate from logs reserved for boards; do not assume a fixed firewood yield. Dropped tree seeds can self-plant after a delay; resin can regrow. Neither is instant.

processSteps.label: Build a matched pair
processSteps.claim: At each trestle position, right-click a stick, another stick, then rope. Build the second directly beside the first, not diagonally. Lay a log across the pair. The pack disables the alternative grid-crafted sawhorse: use this in-world assembly.

processSteps.label: Saw boards or beams
processSteps.claim: From an end, hold right-click with a saw; select planks or beams in tool mode. Normal saws are allowed; keep matching logs for continuous feeding. For tannin instead, strip the side using a bark spud or axe with an offhand hammer. Use fresh tanning bark, or dry and quern it for the alternative barrel recipes.

processSteps.label: Spend boards on capability
processSteps.claim: Build a Toolsmith workbench for assembly and a grindstone for maintenance. Their native recipes use planks; the workbench also needs a saw, while the grindstone needs an appropriate rock. Continue into the existing Toolsmith guides rather than replacing its handles, grips, bindings or treatments with ordinary grid tools.

processSteps.label: Automate after the hand route works
processSteps.claim: A sawmill needs its frame, carriage, sash, crankshaft, feed levers and blade kit, plus an axle driven by mechanical power. Use its native page for assembly and feeding. Do not craft a bare frame and expect it to cut.

processSteps.label: Find and prepare ore
processSteps.claim: Use prospecting to locate deposits, then bring back ore chunks. ImmersiveOreCrush adds in-world crushing by striking chunks on the ground. Start with a hammer and check the interaction prompt. Do not treat every mineral as interchangeable: keep smelting ore separate from quartz, borax and pigments for the materials workshop.

processSteps.label: Make the first usable metal
processSteps.claim: Prepare charcoal and fired clay equipment. Follow Smelting for crucible charges, fuel and casting. Make copper ingots or castable heads as appropriate; follow the live alloy recipe when moving to bronze. Do not put iron ore through a copper casting workflow.

processSteps.label: Shape a head, then assemble
processSteps.claim: Use Smithing for anvil work and Toolsmith's crafting-method guide for the matching modular assembly. Prioritize mining and sawing capability to expand the workshop. The Toolsmith workbench, component choices and maintenance remain part of this route; a head alone is not your finished tool.

processSteps.label: Cool, maintain, then progress
processSteps.claim: Manual Quenching adds cooling hot metal without dropping it; consult Quenching for the actual mechanic, not an assumed universal stat bonus. Repair and maintain tools using Toolsmith's own instructions. Move through the native iron and steel progression only when you have the required fuel, furnace and forging setup; use Reforging when recovering Toolsmith metal parts. Armour-quenching compatibility is item-specific; do not assume every armour piece accepts the same treatment.

processSteps.label: Set up the powder bench
processSteps.claim: Prepare a pulverizer, quern, barrels, water and high-temperature fuel. The native guide describes crushing minerals and then grinding them into powders. Reserve powdered quartz for glaze base and frit; keep coloring powders separate from metal intended for smelting.

processSteps.label: Mix a clear base
processSteps.claim: In a barrel, combine water with supported clay to make clay slurry. Add powdered quartz to slurry for clear glaze base. Follow the barrel recipe for quantities; milky base is a different branch using powdered cassiterite.

processSteps.label: Bake and grind a blue frit
processSteps.claim: For the copper-based blue option, mix lime, powdered copper, powdered quartz and powdered borax using the shown grid recipe. Heat the frit mix into baked frit, then grind it into ground frit. Ground pigment is not yet finished glaze.

processSteps.label: Rest, coat, and fire again
processSteps.claim: Combine clear base and ground blue frit in a barrel and seal it for 48 hours. Coat a fired bowl using the glazing-bowls barrel recipe, then fire the raw glazed result. The finished glazed bowl is a meal and liquid container; stop here before branching into stamps, tiles or colored glass.

processSteps.label: Keep working stock visible
processSteps.claim: Stack fuel and boards near the woodworking and metal stations, leaving room to use the machines. Ground storage is the first option, not a substitute for every container. Check the native placement controls before building a wall of inaccessible stock.

processSteps.label: Give bulk inputs a resource bin
processSteps.claim: Craft a Purposeful Storage resource bin from planks. Its shipped restrictions include ore chunks, nuggets and metal bits, charcoal, quartz, sticks and selected powders. Keep separate bins by workflow; it is not an unrestricted chest. Check held descriptions for accepted groups before moving all your stock.

processSteps.label: Separate pantry from workshop
processSteps.claim: Containers Bundle's food cupboard is a functional food-storage branch made from boards and metal nails-and-strips. Its block definition gives vegetable and grain spoilage modifiers; it does not promise the same benefit for every food. Keep pantry storage separate from ore and powders, and still use proper preservation conditions.

processSteps.label: Carry and sort deliberately
processSteps.claim: Carry On is enabled: check its key bindings and container interaction before relocating a loaded store. Sortable Storage adds a sort button to storage containers; use it to tidy a store, not as a promise of automatic routing between stations. Keep input and output stock separate.

processSteps.label: 1. Make a starter walking stick
processSteps.claim: Follow the crude-stick recipe: three sticks on a diagonal, with a rope immediately left of the centre stick (pattern __S / RS_ / S__). Its pack config grants AutoStep and a hunger modifier of -5; unlike better sticks, it has no WalkingSpeed entry. Equip it as a walking aid; the native guide describes passive bonuses while equipped.

processSteps.label: 2. Choose a forgiving route
processSteps.claim: Scout a route home before trying cliffs. Watersheds, Rivers and Terra Prety alter terrain. Climbing is limited to stone and ore; sprint-jumping is disabled. Test the movement controls on low ground before committing to a drop.

processSteps.label: 3. Build a shared waypoint station
processSteps.claim: Make a cartography table using its native recipe. Take the quill by right-clicking the ink-and-quill on the placed table. With the quill, right-click its map to write your changes; Ctrl + right-click reads the table changes into your map. Each table has its own shared waypoints; deletions are copied too.

processSteps.label: 4. Make repeat journeys easier
processSteps.claim: Use the same path repeatedly to develop a trail. Only players create trails here; TrailDevolveDays is 60 and TrampledSoilDevolveDays is 4, so paths are not permanent. For group exploration, the advanced cartography table also shares explored areas; the ordinary table shares waypoints. For hauling, follow the native cart/sled construction recipes; horses have species-specific saddlery. Carry On portability is not vehicle construction.

processSteps.label: 1. Check the water before launching
processSteps.claim: Watch the wind, treetops, darkening sky and swell. Plan a short crossing with a sheltered landing, and turn back as storms approach. Rough Seas describes lightning and dangerous surf; a boat is not a safe place to wait out a storm.

processSteps.label: 2. Pack for the actual vessel
processSteps.claim: Read Vessels and Their Repair, inspect the hull, and take its repair materials plus a bowl or bucket for bailing. Different vessels have different repair requirements; do not assume one repair material works for every hull.

processSteps.label: 3. Do not depend on river propulsion
processSteps.claim: Rivers do not push boats in this pack. Paddling and sculling are faster, but that does not make a hull stormproof. Keep repair materials aboard and avoid damaging the vessel with an axe.

processSteps.label: 4. Moor before stepping ashore
processSteps.claim: With a rope, right-click the vessel and then a fence post ashore. Use the rope tool-mode control to adjust its length; a longer rope permits a wider swing. A sailboat can instead lower its anchor by right-clicking it with an empty hand, and raise it the same way. Storms can drag or break moorings: leave valuables ashore.

processSteps.label: 1. Make a small healing reserve
processSteps.claim: Place two flax twine vertically in the crafting grid to make two clean bandages. Keep them accessible before leaving shelter. The clean bandage is a real healing item, not an ingredient-only preview.

processSteps.label: 2. Check the combat settings
processSteps.claim: Melee swings stop on terrain; spear directional attacks and vanilla armour grid recipes are disabled. Practise in open ground and follow the current equipment recipes. Bellhead alarms can summon enemies; do not expect vanilla enemy behaviour.

processSteps.label: 3. Retreat with a recovery plan
processSteps.claim: Self-revive and passed-out recovery are disabled; the map is hidden while downed. Agree a regroup and rescue plan before splitting up. Drifters can open doors here: an auto-closing door is not a secure recovery shelter.

processSteps.label: 4. Track and recover cautiously
processSteps.claim: Blood Trail adds blood trails to animals wounded by a player. Follow tracks only when the return route and your remaining healing are adequate. Immersive Corpse Drop makes harvested corpse contents drop without a loot UI, so check the ground after harvesting rather than waiting for a container window.

processSteps.label: 1. Found a note currency
processSteps.claim: Craft and place a Coins mint using its native recipe, then right-click it. Choose a name, a 2–4 letter symbol and a colour. Your first personal currency is free. Mint a small quantity of 1-notes first; unlimited minting does not guarantee anyone will accept them. This pack permits at most three currencies per player.

processSteps.label: 2. Store money without hiding your payment
processSteps.claim: Deposit notes by dragging them onto a wallet, or open the wallet and choose Deposit all notes. Withdraw before buying at a note-accepting shop: the Coins guide says shops take loose notes, not wallet balances. Losing the wallet loses its contents.

processSteps.label: 3. Make the exact change
processSteps.claim: A shop asking for five 1-notes will not take a 10-note. Craft one 10-note into ten 1-notes, or one 100-note into ten 10-notes. Different currencies never mix. Use the Coinage guide separately for metal coin-making; no exchange rate between the two mods is established. Coinage requires hammer tool tier 3. Food still decays in Vinconomy shops here (stall perish rate 0.015).

processSteps.label: 4. Coordinate a group
processSteps.claim: At a bound mint the founder can add players under Shared with. They can mint that currency, but cannot rename or transfer it. Use a notice board to advertise issuer, denomination and meeting place; its UI provides Compose notice. Ownership and posting permissions still apply. Tabletop Games is optional social play, not a prerequisite for trading. For Hand to Hand, the config requires the receiver to hold R; one-sided forced handoff is disabled.
